title: Choose the visual world for WordCounter
question: The roll assigned the Compositor's Type Case. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Compositor's Type Case
options.lineage: Wooden California job case of movable type, where each letter occupies a cell sized by its frequency
options.thesis: Your vocabulary is living type: each word occupies a cell sized by how often you set it, and the case fills as you write.
options.viewport: A warm dark oak surface with the type case as the primary composition — cells holding words at frequency-proportional sizes, a brass-ruled ingestion area at the top where new text enters the case.
options.risk: Reads craft-nostalgic when the woodgrain dominates over function.

raised.raise: Cross-check discipline: every metric agrees with every other at a glance, no gauge contradicts its neighbor.
Depth as rank: the most-used words burn brightest, the least-used recede into the grain, no enclosure needed.

options.label: Laboratory Logbook
options.lineage: Bound scientific observation journal with graph paper, timestamped data tables, and running totals
options.thesis: Your vocabulary is an empirical record: every ingestion is a dated observation, every word a specimen with a frequency measurement.
options.viewport: A dark lab bench surface, the logbook open to today's page — a graph-paper grid backing the ingestion form at top, tabulated word observations below with running frequency columns, a red pen annotation system for first-use markers.
options.risk: This is familiar territory — the direction most runs in a measurement category land on.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail map fired as midnight-blue enamel mural
options.thesis: Your vocabulary is a transit network: each word is a station, usage frequency is the line that connects them, and ingestion dates are interchange points.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue enamel ground with word-stations connected by colored frequency lines, interchange circles where active and passive vocabularies meet, a station-search input at top.
options.case: Strong audience identification — learners already think in routes and connections between words. Loses on product clarity: the transit metaphor obscures the core frequency measurement.
options.risk: The transit metaphor carries connections but WordCounter measures frequency, not relationships.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller Queue
options.lineage: Cracktro title screen with bitmap face over emissive black void, parallax dust fields, no enclosure
options.case: Deeply committed system but language learners do not identify with demoscene culture. The void is dramatic but hides the measurement clarity this product needs.
options.kept: Depth as rank — brightness and spacing encode frequency without boxes or borders.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.lineage: Small aircraft night instrument panel — six luminous gauges for cross-check trust
options.case: The cross-check metaphor is powerful for a measurement tool, but the aviation world is foreign to language learners. Gauges work for 6 values, not 500+ words.
options.kept: Cross-check scan discipline — every metric visible and in agreement at one sweep.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark dashboard with indigo/emerald accent cards, zinc surfaces, and a data table — what every vocabulary tracker ships.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects: metric cards at top, text area in the middle, sortable word table below. Full craft, zero surprise.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the current WordCounter and every other dark-theme dashboard.
